exposure: Presence or absence of SARS-CoV-2 placentitis
cohort: 116 women who had a verified SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy and gave birth between April 2020 and February 2022 in the Stockholm region, Sweden
finding: SARS-CoV-2 placentitis was present in one-fifth of the examined placentas and was associated with a shorter time gap between maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and delivery, a higher rate of acute caesarean section due to fetal indication, and one case of stillbirth.
mod_finding: 86.4% of women with SARS-CoV-2 placentitis underwent acute caesarean section (ACS), all on fetal indication, compared to 50% of women without placentitis who underwent ACS on fetal indication.
